title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues a 'Scholie' (begun on p.106) comparing two axiomatizations of a 'topology without points'. Grothendieck calls them 'magasins'. Both carry the order relations ≤ (inclusion) and ≪ (well-inside / relatively compact inclusion). They differ in the third primitive. In the first it is the overlap relation ≬ (X ≬ Y: X and Y meet, roughly). In the second it is a disjunction relation |∘| (X |∘| Y: X and Y are intrinsically disjoint, roughly 'separated').

From p.106:
- A ≬-magasin yields |∘| by (*): X |∘| Y iff all open pieces x ∈ ouvb(X)°, y ∈ ouvb(Y)° satisfy x ∥ y.
- A |∘|-magasin yields ≬ by (**).
- |∘| can be recovered from the ≬-structure it generates only under Mag 6''. This is a 'divisibility' condition on addition (union), equivalent to (****): X |∘| Y iff x |∘| y for all x ∈ ouvb(X)°, y ∈ ouvb(Y)°. In other words, |∘| is determined by a relation on the sublattice L of 'open' elements.

On this page Grothendieck shows that (****) implies the 'atomic' axioms AtL1, AtL2, AtL3:
- AtL1: ouvb(X)° ≠ ∅ for every X ∈ M. If ouvb(X)° were empty, (****) would hold vacuously and give X |∘| X. This is excluded by Mag 5'', the anti-reflexivity of |∘|.
- AtL2 follows via (***).
- AtL3 follows via a corollary of Mag 4''.
- Moreover the axiom AtC(spec) seems to hold automatically. Without (****) it is doubtful.

Conversely, take a ≬-magasin satisfying AtL1–L3; these allow |∘| to be defined naturally. Its ≬ coincides with the ≬' defined from that |∘| iff M satisfies AtC(spec).

Hence on the common domain there is an equivalence of categories: {≬-magasins with AtL1, L2, L3, AtC(spec)} ⇔ {|∘|-magasins satisfying (****)}. Both notions are thus two generalizations of one species of structure. Grothendieck judges that common structure too restrictive because of AtL1, i.e. the requirement that every element have nonempty interior.

On p.108 he concludes that the |∘| approach is richer. It carries an intrinsic notion of disjunction reflecting geometric intuition, and it makes the earlier axioms AC(Σ…) look artificial.

In modern terms: this is pointless / lattice-theoretic topology aimed at 'tame topology', comparing an overlap-based and a contact- (separation-) based primitive. (****) says the contact relation is generated by its restriction to a base of open elements.
errors: The deduction of AtL1 from (****) is correct but depends on vacuous quantification together with anti-reflexivity (Mag 5''). It is fine, provided Mag 5'' is assumed for all X in M, including any 'empty-like' elements; whether M contains an empty element is not addressed.
AtC(spec) is only said to 'seem' to hold automatically under (****); no proof is given.

The equivalence of categories is asserted 'visiblement' without checking morphisms. In particular it is not checked that the two constructions (*) and (**) are mutually inverse on morphisms, not just on objects.

ideas.what: Two primitive-relation axiomatizations of point-free (tame) topology, one by overlap (≬) and one by disjunction/separation (|∘|), and their comparison
ideas.modern_name: mereotopology / contact algebras vs overlap-based mereology; proximity (contact) relations
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitehead, de Laguna (1920s); Clarke (1981); Randell–Cui–Cohn RCC (1992); Dimov–Vakarelov contact algebras (2000s); Efremovich proximity spaces (1950s)
ideas.where_published: Only the general program of tame topology appears in Esquisse d'un programme (1984, §5); the 'magasins' axiomatics is unpublished as far as I know

ideas.what: Condition (****) / Mag 6'': the disjunction relation is determined by its restriction to open elements (a 'divisibility' condition on union)
ideas.modern_name: contact relation generated by a base / regular-open determination of contact
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure (analogous conditions appear in contact-algebra representation theory)

ideas.what: Equivalence of categories between overlap-structures satisfying atomic axioms and disjunction-structures satisfying (****)
ideas.modern_name: equivalence between overlap-based and contact-based mereotopological frameworks under regularity assumptions

missed.claim: In 1986 Grothendieck independently develops, for tame topology, the same comparison that mereotopologists and contact-algebra theorists later studied: overlap vs contact as primitives. He gives an explicit criterion ((****) plus AtC(spec)) under which the two are categorically equivalent. He also deliberately prefers the contact/disjunction primitive precisely because it does not force nonempty interiors (AtL1). This link between Grothendieck's 'analysis situs' notes and the mereotopology / contact algebra / proximity literature seems not to have been made.
missed.quote: Dans les ≬-magasins et les |∘|-magasins, on reconnaît comme deux généralisations d'une même espèce de structure. Celle-ci paraît trop restrictive à mon sens, par la seule présence de AtL1.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It could inform o-minimal / tame-topology foundations and point-free topology. Grothendieck's choice of a disjunction primitive without an interior-nonemptiness axiom parallels debates in region-based theories of space, and may suggest an axiomatics of tame spaces not yet explored.

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains an unpublished, fairly careful axiomatic comparison with an equivalence-of-categories statement. It anticipates or parallels mereotopology and contact algebras, but the mathematics is modest and similar comparisons exist independently in the literature.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: 'amb(X)°' should read 'ouvb(X)°' (consistent with (****) and the vacuous-quantifier argument), both occurrences.
'Mag 5'' (contiguïté[?] transitivité[?] de |∘|)' likely reads '(antiréflexivité de |∘|)', which is what the argument requires.
'≰-mégation(s)' throughout should be '≬-magasin(s)'; likewise '|∘|-mégations' should be '|∘|-magasins'.
'Et l'axiome AtC(spec) semble[?] ... valable' likely reads 'Et l'axiome AtC(spec) devient automatiquement valable'.
'ssi celle-ci[?] ...' likely 'ssi celle-ci (ou M) satisfait AtC(spec)'.
'visiblement par l'équivalence de catégories' likely 'visiblement une équivalence de catégories'.
